nl-kavelruil.name: Netherlands — voluntary urban land exchange (kavelruil)
nl-kavelruil.note: Every party agrees. The exchange is then set down in a notarial deed and registered with the Kadaster; at least three parties take part.

tw-owner-organized.name: Taiwan — owner-organized urban land readjustment
tw-owner-organized.note: Counts private owners and private land only. Land for public facilities and costs may take at most 45% of the area (an exception procedure exists).

kr-association.name: South Korea — urban development association
kr-association.authority: the designating authority’s authorization of the association
kr-association.note: These tests authorize forming the association; the replotting plan has its own later approval.

es-ct-basic.name: Catalonia — basic compensation
es-ct-basic.authority: the municipality’s approval of the compensation project
es-ct-basic.note: Owners of more than half the area can start it; owners who do not join have defined roles.

es-ct-concertacion.name: Catalonia — compensation by agreement (concertación)
es-ct-concertacion.note: Owners of more than a quarter of the area can start it; the municipality then runs a selection.

es-md-compensation.name: Madrid — compensation by the owners
es-md-compensation.note: At least half the area: exactly half is enough here, unlike Catalonia.

co-readjustment.name: Colombia — urban action unit / land readjustment
co-readjustment.authority: approval by the municipal planning authority
co-readjustment.note: Owners of 51% of the committed area; the project also needs more than one participant.

jp-association.name: Japan — landowners’ association
jp-association.note: Three tests at once: owners, leaseholders, and owned plus leased area. Public land is outside them. Land is reallocated by value; reserve land can be sold to fund the works.

jp-joint.name: Japan — individual or joint implementation
jp-joint.authority: the prefectural governor’s approval of the plan
jp-joint.note: Every owner and leaseholder consents; some other rights are exempt.

de-umlegung-new.name: Germany — Umlegung, land developed for the first time
de-umlegung-new.authority: the Umlegung authority’s adoption of the readjustment plan
de-umlegung-new.note: No owner vote: the authority orders and decides, and owners are heard. Distributed by area, no owner gives up more than 30% of their land for public facilities (§58); by value, the gain is settled in money.

de-umlegung-developed.name: Germany — Umlegung, already developed land
de-umlegung-developed.authority: the Umlegung authority’s decision on the readjustment plan
de-umlegung-developed.note: No owner vote: the authority orders and decides, and owners are heard. Distributed by area, no owner gives up more than 10% of their land (§58).

tr-article-18.name: Turkey — article 18 readjustment
tr-article-18.authority: the municipality’s decision on the parcellation plan
tr-article-18.note: No owner consent is needed. Each holding gives up at most 45% of its area for public uses (DOP); the law applies it per parcel.

in-gj-tps.name: India, Gujarat — town planning scheme
in-gj-tps.authority: the State government’s sanction of the scheme
in-gj-tps.note: The authority prepares the scheme and hears written objections; final plots are reconstituted by valuation.

mcpPrivacy.title: MCP privacy policy
mcpPrivacy.intro: This notice covers the Urban Game Theory hosted MCP service, its planning plugin, private preview links and feedback reports. Urban Game Theory operates Consensus Builder. Your AI assistant provider has its own privacy policy for your conversations.
mcpPrivacy.requests: We process the tool arguments your assistant sends: for example place searches, site coordinates, parcel or design identifiers, design geometry, titles and proposed changes. We use them to retrieve data, create and edit drafts, compare alternatives and return results. The MCP service does not request your full chat history or account credentials, and does not itself call a language model or train one.
mcpPrivacy.drafts: Draft content is kept in temporary server-side storage. References normally expire 24 hours after creation or refresh; expired records are removed when storage is pruned. Availability is not guaranteed. Anyone with the full private reference can read its content. These links are not account-protected or end-to-end encrypted: keep them private. Service administrators can access data held by the service.
mcpPrivacy.public: Publishing a design or plan requires explicit confirmation. Published content and any names, descriptions or other data you put in it become public. Content-addressed storage and third-party copies can persist; we cannot guarantee removal of every published copy. The hosted MCP does not sign wallet transactions or make payments.
mcpPrivacy.feedback: When you submit feedback, we store your report text, optional page link, report type, source, receipt identifier, timestamps and notification-delivery state in a private maintainer inbox. A report excerpt and optional page link are sent to the maintainer through Telegram. Feedback has no automatic expiry currently configured and may remain until a maintainer removes it. Include only information you want to share; do not submit passwords, wallet secrets or private chat transcripts.
mcpPrivacy.providers: Hosting, Cloudflare and other delivery infrastructure may process connection and diagnostic data such as IP addresses, requested URLs, timestamps, user-agent information and errors. Place and site queries can reach the configured geodata providers; opening a preview can contact map and imagery providers. Public publication uses the configured content-storage provider. Telegram processes feedback notifications under its own policies. The plugin package itself contains no analytics or executable hooks.
mcpPrivacy.retention: Operational log and backup retention follows the infrastructure configuration; this notice does not promise a fixed deletion deadline for those copies. The privacy page stores its language preference locally in your browser. Your assistant provider may independently retain conversations and tool results according to its own settings and policies.
mcpPrivacy.contact: Use the feedback form below to contact the maintainer about privacy, access, correction or deletion of data we control. Include a report receipt or other reference so we can identify the record. Requests are reviewed against the information available and the limits of public and third-party storage. Future changes to this notice will be dated on this page.

parcelReport.lede: An evidence-based view of the registries we have found, the cities we have checked, and the places still to investigate.

parcelReport.snapshot: Research snapshot: {date} · Population and area estimates: 2025
parcelReport.coverageTitle: How much of the world is represented?
parcelReport.coverageIntro: The measures below describe the jurisdictions in which registry evidence was found.
parcelReport.scopeText: A working source or two successful regional samples do not establish complete coverage. We have not mapped the union of registered parcels. These percentages measure jurisdictions with evidence, not the fraction of land registered or available in the app.
parcelReport.builtUpNote: Built-up surface is a proxy for where structures stand. It includes non-residential buildings and does not measure all inhabited land.
parcelReport.metricLabel: in jurisdictions with national, local or partial registry evidence
parcelReport.breakdownCaption: Jurisdiction evidence, weighted by area and population
parcelReport.denominatorNote: Baselines: {land} km² assigned to JRC land classes, {built} km² of built-up surface, and {population} people. Statistics are available for {count} jurisdictions. Antarctica has no statistical row in this baseline.
parcelReport.cityIntro: Checked cities and queued candidates, including the largest-city and fastest-growing-city lists.
parcelReport.sortHint: Click any column heading to sort; click again to reverse.
parcelReport.cityNote: In the “Registry found” column, “No” means no registry was established by the recorded checks. “Unknown” includes incomplete or unavailable checks. “Implied parcels tried” refers to documented tests of inferred parcel generation; missing records are shown as “Not recorded.” “Yes” may refer to a local registry office or cadastral maps; the separate sample label indicates verified polygons. Click a linked status for a source.
parcelReport.populationNote: Population: UN WUP 2025 urban centres. Growth: estimated average annual population change, 2015–2025. An urban centre may split one municipality or span several, so these values are not municipal or metropolitan totals. Missing or uncertain matches remain blank; hover over an estimate for its matched place.
parcelReport.populationMatch: Matched UN urban centre: {name}. 2025 source plausibility: {quality}.
parcelReport.rosterNote: {count} entries: the UN M49 roster, Taiwan, Kosovo and five separately listed de facto territories. Statistical overlaps are excluded from totals.
parcelReport.countryNote: A national registry can be gated, viewer-only or sampled. “Yes” establishes its identification, not full territorial coverage or open access. Dependencies and supplementary territories are listed separately; overlapping areas are not counted twice.
parcelReport.methodResearchText: A recorded investigation counts, including a failed request. Check dates come from the linked investigation, not from the date this report was built. An identified source and a verified parcel response are tracked separately.
parcelReport.methodGrowthText: The UN average annual rate is 100 × ln(population in 2025 / population in 2015) / 10. It describes historical estimates. Forecasts are not mixed into this column, and missing values are never treated as zero. The growth cohorts require at least 50,000 people in both years and Moderate or High 2025 estimate plausibility; ranks refer to UN urban centres.
parcelReport.methodAreaText: Each statistical jurisdiction belongs to one evidence category. Its area and population are summed in that category and divided by the dataset’s world total. National evidence takes precedence over local evidence; unidentified or missing amounts remain unresolved.
parcelReport.methodLimitsText: The actual extent, completeness and freshness of cadastral polygons. Registry discovery cannot establish that every parcel is registered, downloadable, publicly accessible or supported by the app.
parcelReport.footer: A research inventory. Every conclusion retains its scope.
parcelReport.qualityPopulation: {matched} of {total} city rows have a matched UN population estimate; {growth} have a usable 2015–2025 growth rate. Unmatched places are retained with blank estimates.
parcelReport.qualityRegistry: {found} city rows identify a registry; {verified} have a recorded verified parcel sample. These are separate findings.
parcelReport.qualityDates: {missing} checked city rows have no recoverable check date. Their dates remain blank.
parcelReport.qualityWiki: {linked} city rows have a verified Wikipedia link. A blank link does not establish that no article exists.
parcelReport.qualityArea: JRC area is the area assigned to Degree of Urbanization classes, including rural land. It is not an inhabited-area mask or a measurement of cadastral coverage. Built-up surface measures residential and non-residential structures.
parcelReport.qualityInferred: Only documented inferred-parcel experiments are marked Yes. The research inventory does not contain a complete historical log of such experiments.
parcelReport.qualitySamples: {count} country records passed a two-region sampling test. This is evidence of a service operating in those samples; its nationwide completeness was not reviewed.
parcelReport.qualityRoster: Supplementary territories are listed for discoverability without asserting a political status. Their overlapping land and population are not added to the statistical parent totals.
